title: Unnati Sharma Wins Judo Bronze at Commonwealth Games 2026 in Dominant Glasgow Display
excerpt: The 23-year-old from Uttarakhand defeated South Africa's Skye Knoester by Ippon in 67 seconds as India delivered its strongest-ever judo performance at the Games.
body:
• Unnati Sharma won bronze in the women's 63kg judo event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, defeating South Africa's Skye Knoester by Ippon in just 67 seconds.
  • The 23-year-old from Uttarakhand credits the Inspire Institute of Sports (IIS) in Karnataka as the turning point in her career.
  • India's judo contingent delivered its strongest-ever Commonwealth Games performance, winning two golds, one silver, and two bronzes.
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally congratulated Sharma, calling her commitment and determination "clearly visible."

Unnati Sharma clinched bronze in the women's 63kg judo event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on August 1, capping India's strongest-ever judo performance at the quadrennial event with a dominant Ippon victory over South Africa's Skye Knoester that took just one minute and seven seconds.

The 23-year-old judoka from Uttarakhand dispatched her opponent with a perfectly timed leg hook, sending Knoester onto her back for the highest possible score in judo. It was a clinical finish to a campaign that saw Sharma navigate a tough draw with composure and precision.

The Road to the Podium

Sharma entered the competition with intent. In the Round of 16, she dispatched Eswatini's Lamulela Magagula in one minute and 39 seconds via Ippon, executing two successive waza-aris in a clinical display. She carried that momentum into the quarterfinals, overcoming New Zealand's Qona Christie with a yuko followed by a decisive waza-ari.

A semifinal defeat interrupted her run at gold. Sharma later admitted the loss stung. "It was a missed opportunity for me; I could've won gold had I not made a mistake in the semi-final," she told NDTV. "When I lost, I did feel that the gold had slipped away. But I also wanted to ensure that I did not lose out on the bronze — winning bronze is also a big thing."

"When I won the bronze medal, I was in a bit of shock. Then I felt very happy that I've finally won a medal. I got a bit emotional as well, but at the end of the day, I was just really, really happy."

— Unnati Sharma, speaking to NDTV

From Uttarakhand to the World Stage

Sharma's path to the Commonwealth podium began in modest circumstances in Uttarakhand, where training facilities are basic at best. The turning point came in 2018 when she joined the Inspire Institute of Sports (IIS) in Karnataka, gaining access to world-class coaches and infrastructure that transformed her career.

"Joining Inspire Institute of Sports was the turning point of my career," she said. "At my home in Uttarakhand, we have very basic facilities. When I came to IIS in 2018, I've been able to deliver the best performances of my career. If anyone apart from my family and coaches have a major role in this bronze, it's Inspire Institute of Sports."

Her international pedigree was already growing before Glasgow. Sharma won a silver at the 2023 Asian Open in Kuwait, bronze at the 2025 Asian Open in Hong Kong, and gold at the 2026 African Open in Dakar — a progression that signalled she was ready for the Commonwealth stage.

India's Judo Revolution

Sharma's bronze was part of a historic haul for Indian judo at the Glasgow Games. Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh claimed gold medals, Yamini Mourya secured silver, and Sharma added bronze — giving India four medals in a discipline where it had previously struggled to make the podium at multi-sport events.

The performance drew attention from the highest levels. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Sharma on X, writing: "More glory for India in Judo! Congratulations to Unnati Sharma for winning the Bronze Medal in the Women's 63 kg category at the Commonwealth Games 2026. Her commitment and determination were clearly visible during the games."

India finished the Glasgow Games with 39 medals overall, including 13 gold, with boxing leading the charge.

Eyes on Los Angeles 2028

For Sharma, the bronze is a stepping stone. She and the Indian judo contingent have already set their sights on the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, where India will aim for its first-ever Olympic medal in the sport.

The celebration when Sharma returned home to Uttarakhand told the story of what the medal meant. "People in the neighbourhood came with sweets. Someone brought a dhol. The media came. It was a full-on celebration," she recalled. "Even my school teachers came."

For Indian judo, those celebrations may be just the beginning.
